summary: 新西兰楔齿蜥的独特解剖结构引起了早期研究者的注意。后来对鼠类到达时间和物种分布的研究改变了保护方式，也引出了能否让楔齿蜥重返更多栖息地的问题。
logic: 从国家象征到科学发现
重估鼠类与种群消失的关系
从海岛保护到恢复分布

paragraphs.brief: 新西兰的蜥蜴，即Tuatara，深深地植根于国家的精神之中：今天的象征始于恐龙时代；一种古老的爬行动物，在五分钱硬币的背面被纪念。
sentences: The New Zealand species of lizard, the tuatara, is firmly embedded in the national psyche: an icon for today which dates from the age of dinosaurs; an ancient reptile commemorated on the back of the five-cent coin.
新西兰的蜥蜴，即Tuatara，深深地植根于国家的精神之中：今天的象征始于恐龙时代；一种古老的爬行动物，在五分钱硬币的背面被纪念。
New Zealanders feel an affinity with the tuatara, and accept that active conservation management is required to ensure it will be among the legacies left to future generations.
新西兰人与土阿塔拉人有亲近关系，并承认需要积极进行养护管理，以确保它成为留给后代的遗产之一。

paragraphs.brief: 当欧洲探险家1769年抵达新西兰时，他们发现了两个大岛，他们共同称为大陆，并发现了沿海的许多小岛。
sentences: When European explorers reached New Zealand in 1769 they found two large islands, which together they called the mainland, and many tiny offshore islands around the coast.
当欧洲探险家1769年抵达新西兰时，他们发现了两个大岛，他们共同称为大陆，并发现了沿海的许多小岛。
The naturalists who came with the explorers disregarded the tuatara, though it is improbable none were seen.
与探险者一起来的自然学家无视塔塔拉，尽管不可能看到任何人。
Only several decades later did a tuatara specimen reach the British Museum, where it was eventually classified as just another type of lizard.
几十年后，一个土阿塔拉标本抵达大英博物馆，最终被归为另一种蜥蜴。

paragraphs.brief: 1876年的阿尔伯特·冈瑟(Albert Gunther)是第一批科学家之一，他意识到Tuatara解剖学的一些方面是奇特的——数万年来没有改变。
sentences: One of the first scientists who realised that aspects of tuatara anatomy were odd— unchanged for tens of thousands of years—was Albert Gunther in 1876.
1876年的阿尔伯特·冈瑟(Albert Gunther)是第一批科学家之一，他意识到Tuatara解剖学的一些方面是奇特的——数万年来没有改变。
Gunther believed the tuatara was one of the most valuable objects in zoological anatomical collections, and also noted, in passing, the reptile was likely to become extinct.
Gunther认为，土阿塔拉是动物解剖学收藏中最有价值的物品之一，并且顺便指出，爬行动物很可能灭绝。
From today’s perspective, it is striking that Gunther expressed no concern about the probable demise of the tuatara.
从今天的角度来看，Gunther对塔塔拉的可能死亡没有表示任何关切，这是令人震惊的。
He and his contemporaries were products of their age, strongly influenced by Charles Darwin’s theory, which had only recently been published.
他和他的同龄人都是他们这个年龄的产物，他们受到查尔斯·达尔文理论的强烈影响，而达尔文理论最近才出版。
Their views were something like this: ‘Extinction is a natural process.
他们的观点是这样的：“灭绝是一个自然的过程。
It is sad that species disappear, but that is part of nature.’
物种消失是可悲的，但这是自然的一部分。

paragraphs.brief: Gunther没有认识到这一区别，认为所有老鼠都是最近才引进的。
sentences: There is a second important aspect of Gunther’s work.
Gunther工作的第二个重要方面。
He recorded, correctly, that some of the mammals introduced by Europeans were predators of the tuatara—particularly rats.
他正确地记录了欧洲人引进的一些哺乳动物是塔塔拉的掠食动物，特别是老鼠。

But what he did not realise was that New Zealand has two species of rat, both introduced, both with an appetite for tuatara: the ship’s rat came with European explorers and settlers; but the kiore rat had already been in the country for hundreds of years, brought by Polynesians from the Pacific Islands.
但他不知道的是，新西兰有两种老鼠，两种都有，两者都对塔塔拉有胃口：船鼠与欧洲探险家和定居者一起到来；但基奥拉老鼠已经在国内呆了几百年，是由波利尼西亚人从太平洋岛屿带来的。
Gunther failed to recognise the distinction, believing all rats to be a relatively recent introduction.
Gunther没有认识到这一区别，认为所有老鼠都是最近才引进的。

paragraphs.brief: 在几个岛屿上，土阿塔拉岛人口很少，而且不断减少，这与基奥雷岛有关。
sentences: Little further research was conducted until Ian Crook of the NZ Wildlife Service published his findings in 1973, which can be summarised as follows.
在新西兰野生动物管理局的Ian Crook于1973年公布其调查结果之前，几乎没有开展进一步的研究，这些调查结果可归纳如下。
Tuatara thrive on offshore islands with no rats.
图塔拉在离岸岛屿上兴旺，没有老鼠。
Tuatara never survived on islands with ship’s rats.
图塔拉从没有在岛上靠船鼠生存。
On a few islands, small and declining populations of tuatara occur with the kiore.
在几个岛屿上，土阿塔拉岛人口很少，而且不断减少，这与基奥雷岛有关。
This should not be seen, however, as evidence that tuatara and kiore can coexist.
但是，这不应被看作是Tautara和kiore可以共存的证据。
Rather, Crook proposed, kiore probably only arrived recently on such islands, and thus the small populations represent extinctions in progress.
相反，Crook建议，kiore可能只是最近才抵达这些岛屿，因此，小人口正在灭绝。

paragraphs.brief: 在整个1990年代，理查德·霍尔德韦和他的在惠灵顿维多利亚大学的同事记录了令人惊讶的发现，基奥雷大概是在1800年前抵达的，尽管人们认为新西兰的人口不超过800岁。
sentences: Throughout the 1990s, Richard Holdaway and his colleagues at Victoria University in Wellington documented the surprising discovery that kiore probably arrived about 1,800 years ago, although the human population of New Zealand is thought to be no older than 800 years.
在整个1990年代，理查德·霍尔德韦和他的在惠灵顿维多利亚大学的同事记录了令人惊讶的发现，基奥雷大概是在1800年前抵达的，尽管人们认为新西兰的人口不超过800岁。
How is this possible?
这怎么可能？
Presumably, Holdaway argued, the kiore were brought by Polynesian explorers who visited the country but did not settle.
Holdaway认为，很可能是波利尼西亚探险家带他们来的，但他们没有定居。
Thereafter, the rats were agents of ecological warfare, exterminating perhaps 1,000–3,000 species.
此后，大鼠成为生态战的诱因，灭绝了大约1,000至3,000种物种。
Thus, tuatara and many other species were already rare or extinct when permanent human inhabitants— the Maori—arrived around 1300.
因此，当常住居民——毛利人——大约在1300岁时，Tuatara和许多其他物种已经很少见或灭绝。
This hypothesis is still being debated, but the evidence continues to accumulate in its favour.
这一假设仍在辩论之中，但证据继续积累，有利于这一假设。

paragraphs.brief: 例如，1995年，保护部的Nicola Nelson在蒂蒂岛设立了68个Tuatara。
sentences: Conservation practice has changed dramatically since Crook’s findings were published in 1973.
自1973年Crook公布调查结果以来，养护做法发生了巨大变化。
Eradication of rats from any given environment was believed to be virtually impossible until about 1980, but since then has become routine.
据认为，直到1980年前后，几乎不可能从任何特定环境中消灭大鼠，但从那时起，这种现象已成为司空见惯的现象。
Enormous conservation benefits are accruing as newly rat-free offshore islands are providing sanctuaries for the country’s rarest species.
由于新来的无鼠岛正在为该国最稀有的物种提供保护区，因此，保护利益正在增加。
In 1995, for example, Nicola Nelson of the Department of Conservation established 68 tuatara on Titi Island.
例如，1995年，保护部的Nicola Nelson在蒂蒂岛设立了68个Tuatara。
Since then, four more populations of tuatara have been established elsewhere under similar conditions.
自那时以来，在其他地方，又有4个图阿塔拉人处于类似状况。
Today, numbers of tuatara are still a fraction of what they once were, but for the first time in 1,800 years the decline has been reversed.
如今，楔齿蜥的数量仍远不及当年，但 1,800 年来种群数量持续下滑的趋势首次得到扭转。

paragraphs.brief: 如果我们能把捕食动物从岛屿上引进来为什么不也从大陆上移走呢？
sentences: While the recovery of rare species is itself a good thing, the truly significant outcome of this research is that it liberates the imagination.
虽然稀有物种的恢复本身就是一件好事，但这项研究的真正重要成果是它释放了想象力。
If we can remove predatory introduced mammals from islands, why not from the mainland too?
如果我们能把捕食动物从岛屿上引进来为什么不也从大陆上移走呢？
Perhaps the questions we ask should demonstrate even more visionary ambition.
也许我们提出的问题应该显示更具有远见的雄心。
Can non-mammalian pests also be removed from the mainland?
非哺乳动物的害虫也能从大陆移走吗？
Our rivers, for example, are full of surrogate rats, in the form of introduced species of fish called trout.
例如，我们的河流中充满了代孕老鼠，以引进的鱼类物种形式被称为鳟鱼。
Some day more people will understand that trout have replaced a whole native fauna in our waterways, just as rats replaced tuatara on the mainland.
有一天，更多的人会明白鳟鱼取代了我们水道上的整个本地动物，就像老鼠取代了土卫六一样。
Will such knowledge lead to the creation of mainland ‘aquatic islands’ where we can once again establish those species of indigenous fish that used to live in our rivers?
这种知识是否会导致大陆“水岛”的形成，我们可以再次建立曾经生活在我们河流中的土著鱼类物种？
Similarly, can bellbirds and tuis replace birds like starlings and mynahs?
同样，贝鸟和能取代鸟儿，如星座和神话？

paragraphs.brief: 正如我们不再容忍灭绝一样，我们今后可能不再接受没有我们过去生物奇迹的大陆，例如土阿塔拉。
sentences: The answers to such questions are uncertain, and opposing sides will doubtless be fiercely debated.
这些问题的答案是不确定的，对立方无疑将激烈辩论。
But the role of scientific knowledge in illuminating the past will be crucial.
但是，科学知识在启发过去方面的作用至关重要。
Just as we no longer tolerate extinction, in the future we may no longer accept a mainland devoid of the biological wonders of our past such as tuatara.
正如我们不再容忍灭绝一样，我们今后可能不再接受没有我们过去生物奇迹的大陆，例如土阿塔拉。
Conservation is thus not primarily about the past but about imagining and then creating the future we wish for our children and ourselves.
因此，保护主要不在于过去，而在于想象和创造我们为儿童和我们自己所希望的未来。
For 80 million years until humans arrived, tuatara occurred throughout New Zealand—might they do so again?
在人类到达之前的八千万年里塔拉塔拉在新西兰各地都发生过会不会再次发生？

items.en: What are we told about the Europeans who arrived in 1769?
items.zh: 1769年抵达的欧洲人的情况如何？
correct: They had no interest in the tuatara.
他们对塔塔拉没有兴趣

items.en: What does the writer say about Albert Gunther in the third paragraph?
items.zh: 作者在第三段里对Albert Gunther怎么说？
correct: He was typical of his generation of scientists.
他是他这一代科学家的典型人物

items.en: What did Albert Gunther think about the rats in New Zealand?
items.zh: 阿尔伯特·冈瑟对新西兰的老鼠有什么看法？
correct: There was one species of rat.

items.en: What did Ian Crook conclude from his research?
items.zh: 伊恩·克鲁克的研究结论是什么？
correct: Rats and tuatara cannot live together.

items.en: What were the findings of Richard Holdaway’s research?
correct: Rats caused extinctions before any humans settled.
老鼠在人类安顿之前就造成了灭绝

items.en: The available research supports Holdaway’s theory but it has not been proved.
items.zh: 现有研究支持了Holdaway的理论，但这一理论尚未得到证实。
items.why: 作者承认 Holdaway 的假设 "证据越来越多支持，但仍在讨论",即“已有研究支持，但尚未完全证明”。

items.en: Nowadays, it is possible to totally destroy a population of rats on a small island.
items.zh: 现在，有可能完全摧毁小岛上的老鼠群。
items.why: 原文说彻底清除一个环境里的老鼠曾被视为几乎不可能，但约从 1980 年起已逐渐成为常规做法，近海小岛即是保护实例。

items.en: Crook was the first person to recognise the potential of offshore islands as sanctuaries.
items.zh: Crook是第一个认识到近海岛屿作为保护区的潜力的人。
items.why: 作者说明清除鼠类后的近海岛屿能成为珍稀物种的庇护地，却没有把最早认识到这一用途的人确定为克鲁克。

items.en: Tuatara numbers are continuing to fall.
items.zh: 图塔拉的数量继续下降。
items.why: 如今的楔齿蜥数量虽然远低于从前，但原文明确说 1800 年来首次扭转了下降趋势。“数量仍低”不能读成“仍在下降”。

groups.label: 观点判断 · YES / NO / NOT GIVEN

items.en: The most important result of the tuatara research is that it frees our ________.
items.zh: 楔齿蜥研究最重要的成果是，它解放了我们的 ________。
items.why: 研究“解放了我们的想象力?= frees our creative thought (创意思维)。

items.en: For example, there are many similarities between rats and ________.
items.zh: 例如，老鼠与 ________ 有许多相似之处。
items.why: 作者以“外来鲜鱼" 类比老鼠。

items.en: Should we now go further and consider reintroducing ________ to our mainland rivers?
items.zh: 我们是否该更进一步，考虑把 ________ 重新引入本土河流？
items.why: 回到对应内容“这种知识是否会导致大陆“水岛”的形成，我们可以再次建立曾经生活在我们河流中的土著鱼类物种？”，再按题干要求写出答案。

items.en: Perhaps our children will come to believe in the ________ of species, in the same way that our generation refuses to accept ____ (Q40).
items.zh: 也许我们的下一代将会相信物种可以 ________，正如我们这一代不肯接受 ________（Q40） 一样。
items.why: 这里指对物种的复苏 / 复原 (restoration)愿景，下一代或将相信这一复原。

items.en: Perhaps our children will come to believe in the ____ (Q39) of species, in the same way that our generation refuses to accept ________.
items.zh: 也许我们的下一代将会相信物种可以 ________（Q39），正如我们这一代不肯接受 ________ 一样。
items.why: 当代人拒绝接受“物种灭绝"。

groups.label: 选词填空
groups.instructionsZh: 阅读带空格的中译，回想正确词项及其字母。

pairs: 第 9 段 · 第 3 句
第 8 段 · 第 7 句
第 4 段 · 第 2 句
points: 如今的楔齿蜥数量虽然远低于从前，但原文明确说 1800 年来首次扭转了下降趋势。“数量仍低”不能读成“仍在下降”。
研究“解放了我们的想象力?= frees our creative thought (创意思维)。
clauses: New Zealanders feel an affinity with the tuatara, and accept ….
“that active conservation management is required to ensure it will be among the legacies left to future generations”补足 accept 的内容，交代究竟在说、判断或发现什么。
先读 accept 所在的主句，再把 that 后面的内容作为一个整体。
When European explorers reached New Zealand in 1769 they found two large islands, …, and many tiny offshore islands around the coast.
“which together they called the mainland”修饰前面的 islands。先认出先行词，再读从句补充的特征。
读到 which 时，回看 islands，再把修饰信息接回主句。
